description: Masking disrupted the neural signals of integration and inference that make the Kanizsa illusion, while an attentional blink that made the figures unreported left those signals in place (Fahrenfort et al. 2017, as reported by Lamme).
limitations: Reported secondhand in Lamme 2020. The original study, by Fahrenfort with coauthors outside Lamme's group, is not read here.

sources.quote: It was found that masking selectively disrupts the neural processing of integration and inference
